title: Helping a sick Ory at the 1972 New Orleans festival
summary: At the 1972 jazz festival Garland was called onstage and covered Ory's breaks because he was too ill to play.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: here and he got down, he got sick, like, you know, and she wanted to take him to Hawaii, you know, he went on over there to Honolulu, he stay -- just stay, he was laying around here, he was sick and pretty sick, he was, In 1972, we was on the same bill, I played on the same bill with him, in New Orleans, that's it. Festival -- jazz festival.

But he was so sick, he could hardly blow his horn, they said let that man come away, come by himself, you know? So, they hadn't called me and somebody down in the audience, hollered, 'where's Tootie?' Bring on Tootie, and they said, oh, I forgot him. And hollered come on up now, come out Tootie. And I walks on -- strut down the stage and you know, (unintelligible) was up there -- I know he was glad to see me coming out there to help him out, because he tried to play and couldn't play, and somebody hollered, 'bring a glass of water', and a fellow rushed over and got him a glass of water and give it to him, he couldn't do no good, you know? But, I got up there and I played and breaks he supposed to make, I made them you know, cause we understood one another. I know when he's going to fall down, I know when he wasn't going to be able to come through on his breaks, you know. I'd make it you know?
Or he'd be playing, he'd do that, you know --
I'd take it, that was me, you know, we watch one another, you know?
Sure. Well 42 years is a long time to make music together. Sure is. And one always feels better when you have a friend up there. Next to you.
